Script de PowerShell para correr en el A: PowerShell script to run on Active Directory: creates the service account (if it doesn't exist) and generates the keytab with ktpass -crypto All, with the Realm and FQDN below already filled in — avoids the most common manual setup mistake, copying the script from the documentation and forgetting to change those two values to your own.

Trae dos archivos: kerberos-ad-setup.ps1: Includes two files: kerberos-ad-setup.ps1 (review it before running it, like any script that runs with domain admin permissions) and Ejecutar.cmd, a launcher for the first one. Windows blocks any unsigned .ps1 by default, and the .cmd avoids that error without touching the system's execution policy — double-click Ejecutar.cmd, not the .ps1 directly. It includes no password: it asks for it on the console when run and doesn't save it anywhere. Requires the ActiveDirectory module (RSAT) and ktpass on the machine where it runs.
El keytab lo genera el administrador del: The keytab is generated by the Active Directory administrator (for example with ktpass), not SquidManager. It must correspond to the service account with the SPN HTTP/<proxy FQDN> and cover all encryption types (-crypto All), because the real encryption type the KDC will use can't be predicted ahead of time.
